groups.name: Drafting plus PDF
groups.sub: CAD drawing commands alongside markup and measurement.

groups.name: General PDF editors
groups.sub: Full PDF editors that also handle drawings.

groups.name: Reading, notes and sketching

tools.name: Bluebeam Revu
notes: Tool chests of saved markups, a markups list you can sort and export, calibrated measurement and takeoff, sheet comparison and overlay, and Studio Sessions for live review with consultants.

The full desktop app is Windows only. Support for Revu for Mac ended in June 2023; Revu for iPad was withdrawn from sale in December 2025. Mac users can use the web app. Check the mobile feature list before relying on it for site measurement.
tools.meta: Price: US$260 (Basics), US$330 (Core), US$440 (Complete) or US$590 (Max, introductory price) a user a year, billed annually; 14-day free trial. Overlay, compare and full takeoff need Core or above · Also on iPhone, Android · Website

tools.name: Drawboard PDF
notes: Annotate PDFs with pen, shapes, text and signatures. Paid plans add scaled measurement, cloud storage and shared documents for real-time review.
For commercial work, Drawboard specifies Pro Plus or Pro Unlimited. Check the plan terms before using the free tier for project deliverables.
tools.meta: Price: Free. Paid tiers $6.99–13.33 a month, billed annually · Also on Android · Website

tools.name: Caliper
notes: A PDF markup and takeoff app for Mac and Windows from a licensed architect. Set each page’s scale by two points or read it from the printed scale, then measure lengths, areas and angles that snap to the drawing’s own lines. Tagged areas total into a schedule that exports to CSV.

Lay one drawing over another to compare revisions, or open two side by side with scroll and zoom locked together. Markups save into the PDF itself, and files stay on the computer, with no account. After the 30-day trial, marking up stays free, and the license adds saving, printing and export.
tools.meta: Price: $149.99 one-time for each platform, with Mac and Windows licensed separately · Also on the Mac App Store · Website

tools.name: Layr
notes: A drawing review app for Windows, Apple Silicon Macs and the browser. Emphasizes high performance with large sets and commands and shortcuts modeled on the pro PDF tools. Measure and count from a calibrated scale, and read page numbers, sheet names and scales across the set in one pass.

A familiar Bluebeam-style markup drawer, and Bluebeam and Acrobat markups open and stay editable. Shared cloud projects show each other’s markups live, on the desktop or in the browser, and revisions compare in a split screen, though it lacks overlay. After the 7-day trial, editing stops, but files still open, print and save. A license runs on one device at a time.
tools.meta: Price: US$5 a month or US$35 a year for one person, US$30 a user a year for a team with a two-seat minimum; 25 GB of cloud storage per person; 7-day free trial · Website

tools.name: redcolumn
notes: A PDF markup and takeoff app from one developer that runs in the browser or as a desktop app. CAD commands such as Offset, Fillet and Trim work on markups, and an assembly turns one measurement into the materials it needs. Markups save as standard PDF annotations that open in Bluebeam Revu.
Compare clouds every difference between two revisions, and Overlay stacks them in color. Shared live markup through your own OneDrive is experimental.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source · Website

tools.name: SketchWeave
notes: A browser app from designers in Ontario that organizes a drawing set by sheet. Each uploaded PDF page is matched to its sheet and stored as a new version, and the markups carry over to the new version. Built-in 2D CAD, with typed lengths, dimensions that resize the shape, offset and trim, draws the answer to a markup to scale and places it on the sheet.

Every mark has a status, from Markup through backcheck to Done, and each finished round of review is kept as a package. It also tracks QAQC checklists per sheet and merges a submission into one PDF. It works alongside Revit, AutoCAD or Archicad, not in place of them.
tools.meta: Price: CA$5 a month for one person, CA$8 a seat a month for a team; 14-day free trial, and a free view-only account for invited teammates · Website

tools.name: Ncored
notes: A PDF editor for large CAD and BIM drawing sets. Redlines, notes, shapes and large-format printing, with local files.
Set the scale by ratio or by calibrating a known length, then measure lengths and areas. Drag an older revision onto a sheet to overlay it, with additions and removals in color.
tools.meta: Price: €12.99 a month, €79.99 a year, or €159 one-time (limited offer) with updates to the version you buy; 14-day free trial · Website

tools.name: Xodo PDF Studio
notes: Markup, calibrated measurement and document comparison on Windows, Mac and Linux, by subscription or a one-time license. Formerly Qoppa PDF Studio.
tools.meta: Price: US$240 one-time with three years of updates, or US$9.99 a month billed yearly (US$19.99 billed monthly) · Website

tools.name: PDF-XChange Editor
notes: A Windows editor for one person working alone. Clouds, callouts, stamps, and calibrated length, perimeter and area measurement, with measurements exported to a CSV file. The free version includes all of the measuring tools.
The Plus edition compares two documents. It has no shared review.
tools.meta: Price: Free for markup and measurement. Editor US$62 and Editor Plus US$79, one-time, each with a year of updates. Further years of updates cost about 25% of the license price · Website

tools.name: PDFelement
notes: A general PDF editor for Windows, Mac, iPad and Android, with OCR, page editing and conversion. Measures distance, perimeter, polygon area and circle area, and adds up several measurements for you. You set the drawing scale by typing a ratio.
Compare two PDFs side by side with insertions, deletions and changes highlighted. To collect comments from others, share a document by link or email through PDFelement Cloud.
The free version lets you try measurement and comparison for 14 days. After that they need a paid plan.
tools.meta: Price: For Windows only, US$103.99 one-time for version 13, US$63.99 a year, or US$109.99 for two years. Plans that add Mac, iPad and phone cost about US$8–10 more. Prices shown as discounts · Also on iPhone, Android · Pricing · Website

tools.name: PolyPDF
notes: A drawing app for Mac, Windows and iPad from one developer. Callouts, discipline colors, and measurement of lengths, areas, perimeters and angles at a calibrated scale. The desktop apps compare two documents, with a colored overlay in Pro.
The free tier allows three measurements per document. Shared live markup between Mac and Windows users is in beta, through a collaboration server the firm hosts itself.
tools.meta: Price: Free. Desktop Pro $74.95 one-time, iPad Pro $99 one-time · Also on iPhone · Website

tools.name: REVIFF
notes: A revision comparison app for Windows from one architectural designer. Open two versions of a sheet, as PDFs or images, and it clouds each area that changed, with added and removed content in different colors. When the sheets don’t line up, Auto-align corrects scale and offset, and Partial Align realigns one region.

It compares; it does not mark up or measure. The comparison runs on your computer, with no upload, account or watermark. Version 2.0 adds an overlay mode and, as beta features after a one-time sign-in, a review report with a decision and note on each change and optional AI summaries by Claude or Gemini.
tools.meta: Price: Free, on the Microsoft Store · Website

tools.name: KresCAD
notes: A browser workspace from architects in Melbourne. Calibrate a PDF plan, measure lengths and areas, count items, add notes and draw to scale, then export a watermark-free PDF. OCR in seven languages makes scanned plans searchable, and files stay in the browser.

Compare drawings highlights what changed between two revisions, with a slider to check each one. It runs in desktop and laptop browsers, with tablet and phone planned. It does not import DWG or DXF. Its maker calls it experimental and asks you to check measurements against the plan.
tools.meta: Price: Free, no account. Paid options may come later · Website

tools.name: PDF Measure
notes: A browser tool for measuring and marking up PDF plans: lengths, areas, perimeters and angles at a set scale, with counts and runs totaled across sheets and exported to CSV. Clouds, callouts and dimension lines export on a marked-up PDF, and an overlay tints one sheet over another to show changes. DWG and DXF drawings open too, each layout as a sheet at its scale.
Files stay on your device. Symbols are counted by clicking, and it has no unit costs. Markups move between computers as a JSON file, with no shared review.
tools.meta: Price: Free, no account · Website

tools.name: Deta Studio
notes: A drawing review app from architects, for Mac and Windows, with a cloud version in the browser. Calibrate a sheet once, then measure lengths, areas, perimeters and counts to scale, metric or imperial. The desktop app opens and saves PDFs on your computer, offline.

Deta Cloud adds shared drawings with markups that appear live, version history, and takeoff tables built from markups. Contractors and clients open a shared link to view without an account, and sign in to comment. Overlay two revisions to highlight every change, on local PDFs or cloud versions.
tools.meta: Price: Desktop $89 one-time for Mac and Windows, with a 30-day free trial. Deta Cloud is free for up to five documents, then $12.50 a user a month (Pro) or $17 a seat a month (Studio, three-seat minimum), billed yearly · Free desktop license for educators and students · Website

tools.name: PDFScope
notes: A browser viewer for multi-page plan sets: annotate, comment, stamp, fill forms, rotate pages and jump between sheets. Calibrate each sheet, or give a detail its own scale, then measure lengths, perimeters, areas and counts, with totals in tables on the sheet and a CSV export. Pages can be extracted, split and downloaded as a ZIP.
Files stay on your computer, and certificate signing (PAdES) happens in the browser. It compares two sheets side by side, with a swipe, an overlay or as a diff. It has no shared review.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (Apache 2.0), no account · Open PDFScope · Website · Source

tools.name: Project Blueprint
notes: A PDF markup and takeoff app for construction drawings, for Mac and Windows, with Linux in beta. Set each sheet's scale, then measure lengths, areas and counts, with totals exported to CSV.
Overlay two revisions to compare them. Markups save into the PDF, and markups from Bluebeam Revu or Acrobat open for editing. Files stay on your computer.
tools.meta: Price: US$149 one-time with a year of updates, covering any two computers, Mac, Windows or Linux. Founder price of US$19, with every 1.x update, while it lasts · 14-day free trial · Website

tools.name: Notch
notes: A PDF editor for construction and design teams, in the browser and as an app for Mac, iPhone and iPad. Set each page's scale from a standard preset or a known line, then measure lengths, areas, perimeters and counts. Quantities export to a spreadsheet.
Overlay two revisions in tint, diff or fade. Teammates' markups appear live, and a view link opens the latest drawing with no account.
tools.meta: Price: Free for basic markup. Solo $8 a month and Pro $16 a month, billed yearly ($12 and $24 billed monthly), with a 14-day free trial. Pro adds a shared team workspace, with Collaborator seats at $6 a month · Website

tools.name: PlanDiFy
notes: A free PDF reader and editor, in the browser or as a desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux. The browser app also works in Safari on iPad. Full measurement tools at a calibrated scale, including length, area, perimeter and takeoff. Compare revisions with an overlay. Offset or copy shapes and measurements by a set distance. Markups display in other PDF apps.
tools.meta: Price: Free, with optional donations · Website

tools.name: Open PDF Studio
notes: A free, open-source PDF editor for construction drawings, on the desktop, as an Android tablet app and in the browser. Place a scale region, several per sheet if needed, then measure distances, areas, perimeters and angles, and count objects by named category. Measurements total in a quantities schedule that saves as CSV.

Compare two revisions overlaid, side by side or with a swipe line, with additions in green, removals in red and a list of changes. Markups save as standard PDF annotations, each with an author, status and replies. In the browser, your file stays on your computer.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source (LGPL-3.0) · Also on Android · Website · Source

tools.name: RedDraft
notes: A keyboard-driven PDF markup app for Windows, aimed at engineers and architects reviewing drawing sets. Set each sheet’s scale or calibrate from a known dimension, then take lengths, perimeters, areas, angles and counts that snap to endpoints, midpoints and intersections on the drawing’s own linework, with ortho and angle locks as in CAD.

Clouds, callouts, stamps and other markups save as standard PDF annotations, so they open in any PDF viewer and stay editable. A tool chest and block library hold your own symbols, an overlay compares two sheets, and a second window puts plans and sections on separate monitors. Files stay on the computer, with no account. It has no shared review, and the listing describes no takeoff totals or export.
tools.meta: Price: US$49.99 one-time on the Microsoft Store, shown as half off US$99.99 until 30 December 2026; free trial · Website

tools.name: Drawboard Projects
notes: Drawboard’s team product for drawing review. Drawings live in one project with versions, markups sync live, and tasks are pinned to a spot on a sheet with an owner and a status, collected into task lists such as a punch list or RFIs. Overlay stacks up to five revisions in different colors. Clients and consultants join as guests without a paid license.
On a Mac it runs in the browser.
tools.meta: Price: From $29 per user a month, or $270 a year billed annually · Website

tools.name: Adobe Acrobat Pro
notes: A general PDF editor that many firms already license. Comments, drawing markups, calibrated measurement, file comparison and shared review. Measurement and comparison are in the Windows and Mac apps, not the web or iPad apps.
Sort and filter the Comments list by author, page, type or status.
tools.meta: Price: Acrobat Pro US$19.99 a month on an annual plan, US$29.99 month to month, or US$239.88 a year prepaid · Also on iPhone, Android · Website

tools.name: Foxit PDF Editor
notes: A general PDF editor with measurement, file comparison and shared review. Firms often license it for office documents.
tools.meta: Price: About $130 per user a year, $160 with the iPad and phone apps. Foxit PDF Editor 14 is also sold for $209.99 per user, one-time · Also on iPhone, Android · Website

tools.name: Master PDF Editor
notes: A full PDF editor with a native Linux version. Annotations, page editing, OCR, and distance, perimeter and area tools.
You set the drawing scale by typing a ratio. It has no tool for calibrating on a known length.
tools.meta: Price: US$79.95 one-time, with a year of updates; later years of updates cost half. Volume pricing from 10 users · Free trial, which watermarks output · Website

tools.name: PDF Expert
notes: A PDF editor for Mac and iPad with Apple Pencil support. Highlights, shapes, ink, stamps and notes that sync across your devices.
The paid tier calibrates a sheet and measures distance, area and perimeter on Mac and iPad.
tools.meta: Price: US$79.99 a year for Mac, iPad and iPhone, or US$139.99 one-time for the Mac only; 7-day free trial · Also on iPhone · Website

tools.name: Documents
notes: A file manager that opens PDFs with annotation built in. For carrying a set to site, pulling files from cloud storage, and noting what you see on the sheet.
tools.meta: Price: Free; Documents Plus US$9.99 a month or US$49.99 a year · Also on iPhone · Website

tools.name: Morpholio Trace
notes: Sketch a design response over a plan or photo. Set the drawing scale, then dimension it and measure room areas.
Available on iPad and iPhone. It does not provide a shared comment log.
tools.meta: Price: Free tier; Trace Pro US$24.99 a year after a one-month free trial, or US$7.99 a month · Also on iPhone · Website

tools.name: Okular
notes: A document viewer with highlights, notes, lines, shapes and stamps. Stable downloads are offered for Windows and Linux; Mac builds are untested nightlies. No scaled takeoff tools.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source · Website

tools.name: Preview & Markup
notes: Built into Apple devices. Enough to circle something on one sheet and send it back, with nothing to install.
tools.meta: Price: Free, built in · Also on iPhone · Website

tools.name: Xournal++
notes: Handwriting and sketching over a PDF in layers, with pen pressure. Runs on Linux with a drawing tablet.
tools.meta: Price: Free, open source · Website

tools.name: Concepts
notes: A vector sketching app on an infinite canvas, used by architects for concept sketches. Import a PDF plan, set its scale or calibrate on a known length, and sketch and measure over it.
It has no shared review.
tools.meta: Price: Free tier; PDF import needs Essentials, US$39.99 one-time for one platform, or the subscription, US$4.99 a month or US$29.99 a year · Also on Android · Website

tools.name: SVG Editor
notes: A vector illustration editor that runs in the browser. It opens a multi-page PDF as the pages of one drawing, with the linework as editable vectors, and also opens DXF and HPGL plot files. Useful for turning drawings into diagrams and presentation graphics, then exporting PDF, SVG or PNG.

Files stay on the computer, with no account. A measure tool gives lengths, areas and angles in the document’s own units, but it has no drawing scale or calibration, no shared review and no revision compare.
tools.meta: Price: Free, no account · Website

tools.name: PDF Annotator
notes: A long-running Windows app (since 2005) for marking up PDFs with a pen or mouse. Pick a preset or custom scale, or take one from a known dimension, then measure distances, perimeters, areas and angles. Dimensions stay in the PDF.

Symbol, date, signature and custom stamps, plus merging, page numbering and watermarking tools. Markups save into the PDF and open in any viewer. Works offline. No shared review, document comparison or takeoff totals.
tools.meta: Price: US$79.95 per user, one-time, for version 10. Two years of upgrades and support add US$39.94. Volume pricing from five users · 30-day free trial · Website

tools.name: Protakeoff
notes: A takeoff and estimating app for contractors, first released in 2026. Calibrate each sheet or region, then measure lengths, areas with cutouts, and counts, with snapping and ortho lock. AutoCount finds repeated symbols for you to approve. Assemblies of material, labor and waste price the quantities, and the estimate exports to PDF, Excel or CSV.

Blue and red overlays compare revised sheets, and AI renames pages from their title blocks. Works offline. The Team plan adds team sync and a shared template library, but no shared markup is described. On a Mac, you run a Terminal command after installing before the app will open.
tools.meta: Price: Solo US$13 a month or US$120 a year for one user. Team US$76 a month or US$500 a year for six users · 30-day free trial, no card · Website
